statement.p: A rectangular box has a base 8 inches long and 12 inches wide, and the height of the box is 2 inches.
Find the angle between the diagonal of the box and the diagonal of its base. The angle should be measured in radians.

solution.p: Let A be one corner of the base, B be the opposite corner on the base, and C be the point that is directly above B on the top of the box. ABC is a right triangle with right angle at B, and AC is its hypotenuse. AC is also a diagonal of the box, and AB is a diagonal of the base of the box. Therefore angle A of this triangle is the angle that we want.

Its cosine is \displaystyle{\begin{aligned} \cos(A) \amp = \frac{\text{length of }AB}{\text{length of }AC} \\ \amp = \frac{\sqrt{8^2+12^2}}{\sqrt{8^2+12^2+2^2}} \end{aligned} } so \displaystyle{A = \arccos\left(\frac{\sqrt{8^2+12^2}}{\sqrt{8^2+12^2+2^2}}\right) \approx {0.137796} \text{ radians}}.
